title: Account balance cache in a ledger service
name: Ledger balance cache

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code keeps cached balances consistent with the database? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
Two transfers run concurrently: A->B and B->A. What prevents them from deadlocking on the row locks?
choices: The ROLLBACK in the catch block releases locks when Postgres detects the deadlock
Both transactions lock the two rows in sorted account_id order via the SELECT ... ORDER BY ... FOR UPDATE
The conditional UPDATE with available_cents >= $2 never waits on a lock
Each transfer uses its own pooled client, so the locks are independent

questions.prompt: If Redis is unreachable while getBalance() runs, what happens?
choices: get() returns null, the balance is read from Postgres, then set() throws and getBalance() rejects
getBalance() returns null as if the account did not exist
The balance is read from Postgres and returned normally because both cache calls swallow errors
getBalance() hangs until the 300 second TTL elapses

questions.prompt: What does the version column contribute in this code as written?
choices: It is used by set() to refuse overwriting a newer cached balance
It makes the debit UPDATE an optimistic-concurrency check
It is incremented and stored in the cache but nothing compares it, so it does not affect which value wins in Redis
It is used by getBalance() to detect and discard expired cache entries
